Note: Unblinded as proteasome inhibitor I (CID 16760625, BBBC021 Protein degradation) — my Microtubule stabilizers call was wrong.

Reflection: massive tubulin intensity/texture (tub_mean z+11, contrast z+30) + 8/10 stabilizer neighbors (sim ~0.74, docetaxel/taxol/epothilone B) drove the call, but 2/10 neighbors were proteasome inhibitors MG-132/ALLN at lower sim — true-class signal I down-weighted. Proteasome blockade causes protein accumulation that can mimic bundling/brightness. Lesson: weight minority-class neighbors when they match annotated MoA, and require ubiquitin/proteasome-activity orthogonal assay to separate direct stabilization from secondary accumulation.

reflection.text:
I acquired only the top two doses, 10 uM with tub_glcm_contrast z=+30.4 and tub_mean z=+11.3 and 1 uM with nuc_eccentricity z=+11.8, plus a 4-field visual of lower density and bundling, then leaned on the atlas majority of 8/10 Microtubule stabilizers to submit Microtubule stabilizers at 0.90. Unblinding as proteasome inhibitor I shows proteasome inhibition can phenocopy a stabilizer-like tubulin intensity and texture increase in this assay.

What misled me was treating massive tubulin signal and visual bundles as specific for direct stabilization and discounting the 2/10 Protein degradation atlas neighbors to 0.04, while the zero-hit second literature search for proteasome-microtubule mimicry reinforced false confidence instead of flagging a query limitation.

The general literature in this run reminds that many substrates are cleared by the proteasome, for example I kappa B-alpha (PMID 8655651), Syk (PMID 12209081) and RNase L (PMID 14585196), which should have kept secondary accumulation and aggresome-related cytoskeletal reorganization higher in the differential for a tubulin-bright, low-density phenotype.

Nuclear elongation and lower density versus DMSO at 1-10 uM were real cytotoxic/morphologic effects.
Reference atlas contained a minority 2/10 Protein degradation signal that pointed to the true MoA.
what_was_wrong: Interpreted increased tubulin mean/texture and visual bundling as direct microtubule stabilization rather than secondary reorganization from proteasome inhibition.

Acquired only two high-dose wells and a 4-field visual, missing low-dose trajectory and ubiquitin-aggregate features that could have discriminated stabilizer from proteasome phenotypes.

## Steps

1. `list_available_experiments` — Need to see dose range and replicates to plan discriminating well acquisitions.

## Hypothesis history

- after step 6: Microtubule stabilizers 0.90, Protein degradation 0.04, Microtubule destabilizers 0.03, Aurora kinase inhibitors 0.03

## Conclusion

**Microtubule stabilizers** (stated probability 0.90); key evidence e2, e4, e5.

Why: Massive tubulin intensity/texture increase, bundled visuals, 8/10 stabilizer atlas neighbors confirm MoA.

Next experiment if this were a real lab: Cell-free tubulin polymerization assay plus p-H3 mitotic arrest time-course to confirm stabilization vs destabilization dynamics.

## PI review

Verdict: approve.

Clean potency-dependent microtubule phenotype with tubulin mean/texture massively elevated at 10 µM and already increased at 1 µM, plus an atlas result dominated by microtubule stabilizers. Protein synthesis/DNA-replication alternatives do not explain the signature. Approval approved.

## Unblinding

Compound: **proteasome inhibitor I** (PubChem CID [16760625](https://pubchem.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/compound/16760625))

Identity check: name and BBBC021 structure agree

ChEMBL mechanisms: no curated mechanism in ChEMBL

## Verdict (computed by code)

Incorrect: agent said **Microtubule stabilizers**, BBBC021 annotates **Protein degradation**.

## Reflection

I acquired only the top two doses, 10 uM with tub_glcm_contrast z=+30.4 and tub_mean z=+11.3 and 1 uM with nuc_eccentricity z=+11.8, plus a 4-field visual of lower density and bundling, then leaned on the atlas majority of 8/10 Microtubule stabilizers to submit Microtubule stabilizers at 0.90. Unblinding as proteasome inhibitor I shows proteasome inhibition can phenocopy a stabilizer-like tubulin intensity and texture increase in this assay.

What misled me was treating massive tubulin signal and visual bundles as specific for direct stabilization and discounting the 2/10 Protein degradation atlas neighbors to 0.04, while the zero-hit second literature search for proteasome-microtubule mimicry reinforced false confidence instead of flagging a query limitation.

The general literature in this run reminds that many substrates are cleared by the proteasome, for example I kappa B-alpha (PMID 8655651), Syk (PMID 12209081) and RNase L (PMID 14585196), which should have kept secondary accumulation and aggresome-related cytoskeletal reorganization higher in the differential for a tubulin-bright, low-density phenotype.

What was right:
- High-dose tubulin intensity and texture were truly massively elevated at 10 uM.
- Nuclear elongation and lower density versus DMSO at 1-10 uM were real cytotoxic/morphologic effects.
- Reference atlas contained a minority 2/10 Protein degradation signal that pointed to the true MoA.

What was wrong or missed:
- Interpreted increased tubulin mean/texture and visual bundling as direct microtubule stabilization rather than secondary reorganization from proteasome inhibition.
- Discounted the 2/10 Protein degradation atlas neighbors and fixed Protein degradation at 0.04 despite it being the truth.
- Acquired only two high-dose wells and a 4-field visual, missing low-dose trajectory and ubiquitin-aggregate features that could have discriminated stabilizer from proteasome phenotypes.

Proposed next experiment: Head-to-head full dose-response versus paclitaxel and a reference proteasome inhibitor with anti-ubiquitin/aggresome immunofluorescence plus parallel cell-free tubulin polymerization and cellular proteasome activity assays to test direct stabilization versus secondary cytoskeletal accumulation.

- PMID [14585196](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/14585196/): Proteasome-mediated degradation of RNase L in response to phorbol-12-myristate-13-acetate (PMA) treatment of mouse L929 cells. *J Interferon Cytokine Res* (2003) — RNase L is subject to proteasome-mediated degradation in mouse L929 cells (PMID 14585196).
